overall.good: Played close to the spec's ceiling. The notes below are refinements, not faults.

overall.none: This pull was too short or too quiet to grade.

snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.intent: A Re-Origination proc converts your stats for 10 seconds. A Tigereye Brew spent inside it holds those stats for the brew's full 15 seconds, carrying the proc well past its own end. Catching procs is the payoff; catching them late is the refinement.
snapshots.verdict_good: {{caught}} of {{total}} catchable procs taken ({{rate, percent}}). You are playing the pairing.
snapshots.verdict_ok: {{caught}} of {{total}} catchable procs taken ({{rate, percent}}). The procs you missed cost more than how late you brewed on the ones you took.
snapshots.verdict_bad: {{caught}} of {{total}} catchable procs taken ({{rate, percent}}). This is the spec's biggest single lever, and you are mostly not pulling it.
snapshots.verdict_none: No Re-Origination proc arrived with enough Tigereye Brew banked to be worth spending on, so there was nothing to catch.
snapshots.depth_good: They went out {{depth, percent}} of the way into the proc on average — held late, which is where the carry comes from.
snapshots.depth_ok: They went out {{depth, percent}} of the way in on average; holding to the last global would extend each one further.
snapshots.depth_bad: They went out {{depth, percent}} of the way in on average, so most of the proc was spent before the brew froze it.

snapshots.lastGcd_other: {{count}} landed on the final global of theirs.

snapshots.b2b_other: {{count}} procs arrived while a snapshotted brew was still running, so part of each could not be used.
snapshots.givenAway: About {{seconds, seconds}} of proc time went unused across the pull.
snapshots.depthCaveat: Depth averages the procs you caught, not the pull, so it is shown and never graded — on the pulls this was calibrated against, catching two and nailing both scored better than catching twelve.
snapshots.protected_one: One early brew went out with the bank close to full. Holding it to the last global would have pushed {{stacks}} more stacks past the cap, which is worth more than the tail it gave up — so it counts as a decision, not a mistake.
snapshots.protected_other: {{count}} early brews went out with the bank close to full. Holding them to the last global would have pushed more stacks past the cap than the tails were worth, so they count as decisions, not mistakes.
snapshots.tradeMethod: The comparison is in stacks and seconds, both ways. Brewing early gives up seconds of a fifteen-second buff carrying the proc's stats; waiting gives up whatever the bank overflows meanwhile, and each lost stack would have amplified a later brew for its whole fifteen seconds. The larger of the two is what this report calls the mistake.
snapshots.tradeNoMastery: What either side is worth in damage depends on your mastery, and WarcraftLogs does not report one on Mists logs — the field is there and always reads zero. So the trade is weighed in stacks and seconds, and no damage figure is put on it.
snapshots.unaffordable_one: One more proc arrived with too few stacks banked to be worth a brew, so it is not counted as a chance missed.
snapshots.unaffordable_other: {{count}} more procs arrived with too few stacks banked to be worth a brew, so they are not counted as chances missed.
snapshots.narrowlyMissed_one: One of the misses was a brew {{ms, gap}} too late — the proc was read, not ignored.
snapshots.narrowlyMissed_other: {{count}} of the misses were brews that went out just after the proc expired rather than just before, which is a timing problem and not a habit.
snapshots.oneStat: Every proc converted into {{stat}}. The Rune turns your two lowest of crit, haste and mastery into twice the highest, so {{stat}} is what sits on top of your sheet. If that is not the stat you want doubled, change the ordering — reforge, or weave an elixir that lifts another above it.
snapshots.weaved_one: One proc came back as {{stat}} instead of {{held}}, because you swapped an elixir right after the brew went out. Tigereye Brew freezes mastery at the moment it is cast, so that proc was never a snapshot to take. It counts as the play it was, not a chance missed, and is left out of the total above.
snapshots.weaved_other: {{count}} procs came back as a stat the running brew could not hold, because an elixir went out right after each brew. Tigereye Brew freezes mastery at the moment it is cast, so none of them was a snapshot to take. They count as the play they were, not chances missed, and are left out of the total above.
snapshots.unholdable_one: One proc converted into {{stat}}, which Tigereye Brew cannot freeze: the brew’s multiplier reads mastery and nothing else, so there was no snapshot on offer. It is left out of the total above rather than counted as a chance missed.

chiBrew.unknownTalent: This log carried no character snapshot, so the report cannot tell whether you took Chi Brew. It is not saying you did not — it is saying it does not know.
chiBrew.never: You took Chi Brew and never pressed it. The time you spent with something to hit had room for about {{possible}} uses, each worth two chi and two brew stacks.

The cost is priced in chi rather than presses, because a recharge that never ran is a share of one.

debuff.title: Rising Sun Kick
debuff.intent: The debuff is a flat damage increase on everything you and your Storm, Earth and Fire clones do to that target — not the rest of the raid. It runs 15 seconds on an 8-second cooldown, so only a missed global drops it. Uptime asks whether the enemy you were hitting had it, measured against the time you had something to hit — so add waves and phases with nothing in reach never count against you.

chi.intent: Chi waste is a different mistake from energy waste. Energy overflows on a clock whether you are there or not; chi only overflows because you pressed a generator into a bar with no room for what it returned. Every point below cost you a global.

chi.resolution: This bar is reconstructed, not read: WarcraftLogs only reports your chi when you spend it, so the figures come from walking the log forward through what each button gains and costs. Two consequences. A point gained and spent between two readings is invisible, so treat the waste as a floor rather than a total. And spent can exceed gained, because chi you were holding before the log started is paid out here but never counted in.

method.title: Method
method.intent: What was measured and what could not be.
method.engaged: Uptime is measured against engaged time — the pull minus intermissions and time with no target — rather than the raw fight length.
method.energy: Energy is read from the `classResources` snapshot WarcraftLogs stamps onto casts and hits, about three readings a second — not from `resourcechange` events, of which a pull carries around twenty. It is used for time at the cap and nothing else.
method.spec: Classic logs report spec as 0, so the spec is taken from the report's own player list and confirmed by a Tigereye Brew cast.
method.source: One event fetch for report {{code}}, fight {{fightID}}, actor {{actorID}}, straight from your browser to WarcraftLogs.
method.brewStacks: Tigereye Brew stacks are read off the bank aura's removal event, never off the cast — WarcraftLogs logs the drain about a millisecond before the cast, so sampling at the cast reads a bank that has already been spent.
method.dps: DPS is WarcraftLogs' own damage total over the full fight duration.

sef.title: Storm, Earth and Fire
sef.intent: Each press sends a spirit onto an enemy of your choosing, up to two at a time, and it mirrors your damaging abilities onto that enemy. While they are out your own damage is cut — to 60% with one spirit, 45% with two. So it is only worth pressing when there is a second thing to put a spirit on, and once they are out the one way to waste it is to stand on an enemy a spirit already has.
sef.summary_one: {{count}} spirit sent out, out for {{uptime, percent}} of the pull.
sef.summary_other: {{count}} spirits sent out, with at least one of them out for {{uptime, percent}} of the pull.
sef.uptimeMeans: Spirit uptime is the share of the pull, timer to kill, with at least one spirit out. It is not a target to push to 100%, and it cannot tell one spirit from two. A stretch with one enemy calls for no spirit at all, and this figure counts none of that either way. What the pull actually called for is the sentence below about second targets.
sef.prePlaced_one: One spirit was already out when the pull began, placed before the timer started, so it spent no global inside the pull and has no cast row. That is an ordinary opener, not a missing press, and it counts here because the spirit was genuinely out. The press that aimed it is outside this log, so its enemy is read from where it swung.
sef.prePlaced_other: {{count}} spirits were already out when the pull began, placed before the timer started, so they spent no globals inside the pull and have no cast rows. That is an ordinary opener, not missing presses, and they count here because the spirits were genuinely out. The presses that aimed them are outside this log, so their enemies are read from where they swung.
sef.skipped: Storm, Earth and Fire was never pressed, and this pull held a second enemy for {{justified, duration}} in stretches long enough to be worth one — the longest running {{longest, duration}}. That is time two spirits could have spent mirroring you onto something else.
sef.damage: The spirits dealt {{damage, compact}} between them, {{share, percent}} of your damage — already inside your total, because WarcraftLogs files a pet's damage under its owner.
sef.overlap: For {{overlap, duration}} of your {{measured, duration}} in melee with the spirits out — {{share, percent}} — you were hitting an enemy one of your own spirits already had. That is the damage penalty paid for a clone duplicating you instead of spreading you.
sef.overlapWorst: The worst of it was {{target}}, at {{ms, duration}}.
sef.overlapNone: You never shared a target with your own spirits, which is exactly what the cooldown is for.
sef.overlapUnknown: This pull cannot say whether you shared a target with your own spirits: the log carried no separate actor for them, so there is nothing to compare against. Calling that "never" would be a claim the log did not make.
sef.justified: The pull held a second enemy for {{justified, duration}} in stretches longer than {{rule, duration}}, so pressing it was called for.
sef.unjustified: The pull never held a second enemy for longer than {{rule, duration}}; the longest stretch was {{longest, duration}}. Against one target the split is a straight loss.
sef.notGraded: Nothing here reaches your score, and the tiles carry no colour except one. The shared-target tile is a reading aid rather than a verdict: the sim never puts a spirit on the enemy you are hitting, so zero is the mechanic's own answer rather than a bar somebody set. It stops short of a grade because a hard zero would fault the seconds after your target dies and you roll onto one a spirit is holding.

gear.title: Gear
gear.intent: What you were wearing, straight from the log. Item level is here to be read, not judged. The enchants are the part worth acting on: an empty slot costs damage on every pull until it is filled.
gear.none: This log carried no equipment record, so there is nothing to show. Nothing is wrong with the pull — the report was simply not told.

raidBuffs.title: Raid buffs
raidBuffs.intent: The buffs that move a Windwalker's damage, one row per effect rather than one per spell — five classes bring the same attack power and they do not stack, so what matters is whether the effect was on you, not who supplied it. Uptime here is measured against the whole pull, unlike Rising Sun Kick above: a buff stays up perfectly well while the boss is untargetable.
raidBuffs.none: This report was produced before raid buffs were read, so there is nothing to show here. Nothing is wrong with the pull.
raidBuffs.caption: Raid buffs affecting this Windwalker, by effect

worth.stats: Agility is attack power and critical strike at once, which makes this the broadest of the six.
worth.attackPower: A flat multiplier on everything you hit with. Ten percent, not the five it is often quoted as.
worth.meleeHaste: Auto-attack speed only. It does not feed your energy bar, whatever the tooltip suggests.
worth.spellHaste: It shortens the Fists of Fury channel and hands that time back to the list. It does not move energy regen — that runs off haste rating from gear.
worth.crit: Flat critical strike chance, and the one most likely to be missing without anyone noticing.
worth.mastery: Flat rating, so what it is worth to you depends on how you have reforged.

raidBuffs.late: Not up at the pull — it went out {{seconds, seconds}} in.
raidBuffs.gaps_other: Off you {{count}} times, for {{seconds, seconds}} in total.
raidBuffs.notReportedNote: {{buffs}} produced no entry in this log at all. That is not the same as missing, so it is not printed as nought: a buff applied before the pull that never drops emits no event all fight, and the log's own snapshot at the pull is not a complete list. The honest answer is that the log did not say — your raid's buff list is the place to settle it.
raidBuffs.self_one: {{buffs}} is one you supply yourself, and it was not up for the whole pull. That is the one row on this page you can fix alone.
raidBuffs.self_other: {{buffs}} are yours to supply, and they were not up for the whole pull. Those are the rows on this page you can fix alone.
raidBuffs.deaths_one: You died once in this pull. A corpse holds no buffs, so a gap that lines up with it is the death rather than anyone forgetting to buff.
raidBuffs.deaths_other: You died {{count}} times in this pull. A corpse holds no buffs, so gaps that line up with those are the deaths rather than anyone forgetting to buff.
raidBuffs.excluded: Stamina and spell power are left out on purpose. Both are real raid buffs and neither adds a point of Windwalker damage, so a row for either would be one nobody can act on.
raidBuffs.debuffs: The two target debuffs a melee cares about — weakened armour and physical vulnerability — are not on this page, and not because they were missing in the raid. The fetch is scoped to you, so a debuff another raider puts on the boss is in neither what you cast nor what was cast on you. Reading them would take a second query this report does not make uninvited.

rotation.title: The rotation
rotation.intent: The priority list every section above judges you against. Nothing here is graded and none of it is about your pull — it is the reference for when a number comes back wrong.
rotation.economy: Two things shape the list. Your global cooldown is a flat second — haste never shortens it, because none of these is a spell; haste buys energy instead. And chi comes slower than globals: Jab costs 40 energy for 2 chi, and energy refills at about ten a second, so a global earns you two thirds of a chi. Two presses in three have to be chi-free. The rest is ceilings. Energy caps at 100 and the bank at 20, and nine entries do nothing but check the bar is not about to overflow. A full bar regenerates nothing.

flow.title: The priority flow
flow.intent: Read down and press the first thing that is true. There is no second list for packs — the same rungs are read at one enemy and at six, and only how far down you get changes.
flow.caption: The priority list, in the order the rotation checks it
flow.reading_single: This is the list at one enemy, which is how the report is reading your pull. Rungs that need two or more enemies are not drawn, and split rungs show only the half that applies. The chips above still name every count where something changes — the control at the top switches the reading.
flow.reading_multi: This is the list at three enemies, the count every press above is judged at. The single-target half of each split rung is not drawn, and neither is the Spinning Crane Kick that needs four. The chips above still name every count where something changes — the control at the top switches the reading.

legend.title: How to read it
legend.spine: Every rung is one question. Yes: press the button beside it and stop there. No: follow the line down to the next question.
legend.gate: A chip across the line is a gate: below the count on it, the question underneath is never asked.
legend.fork: A dashed box is one question with two or three answers. Only one is ever yours, and the line above says what decides.

crossover.title: Where the pack changes the button
crossover.sck: 3+ · Crane Kick over Fists of Fury
crossover.sckOverRsk: 4+ · Crane Kick over Rising Sun Kick

tigereyeBrew.title: Do you have the Rune of Re-Origination?
tigereyeBrew.detail: One button, two rule sets, and the trinket in your bag picks between them. A stack costs three chi and a brew spends ten, so the bank fills slowly — the branches disagree only about whether anything is worth waiting for.

talent.title: Which of the three you took
talent.detail: One talent row, so only one of these is ever on your bar. All three do the same job: a global that costs neither chi nor energy, taken only when the bar has room to spare. Their order never comes up, because you can only have brought one.

blackoutKick.title: How much the dump has to leave behind
blackoutKick.detail: One entry with two energy reserves in it, and the size of the pack picks between them: how much has to stay in the bar depends on what else there is to spend it on.

risingSunKick.title: Whether the pack has pushed the kick down the list
risingSunKick.detail: One entry with an "or" in it, and the target count decides which half applies. Up to two enemies the kick is pressed on cooldown. From three, the buttons above it beat one kick, and only the debuff running out still claims this rung.

touchOfDeath.name: Touch of Death
touchOfDeath.test: the target's health drops below yours
touchOfDeath.when: the target's health falls below yours.
touchOfDeath.why: It deals a lump equal to your own maximum health, for one global. The list presses Fortifying Brew in the same breath, because that raises the number it rolls against.

chiBrew.name: Chi Brew
chiBrew.test: 2 chi below cap, in the opener or under a brew
chiBrew.when: you are two chi below the cap, during the opener or with a brew running and energy at least four seconds from full.
chiBrew.why: Two chi for no global. Those two chi save you a Jab, and a Jab you skip is 40 energy left in a bar that was already close to full.

tigereyeBrewRune.name: Tigereye Brew
tigereyeBrewRune.test: a proc is a global from ending and the bank beats it
tigereyeBrewRune.when: the Re-Origination proc is a global from ending and the bank holds more than the buff you are already wearing. Failing that: at a full 20 stacks, above 15 with no proc running, or with the fight ending inside the buff.
tigereyeBrewRune.why: With the Rune on, the brew is a snapshot tool and little else. It reads your mastery once and holds it fifteen seconds, so spending it on the proc's last global is what makes the proc's stats outlive the proc — see below. Every other condition stops the bank overflowing while it waits.

tigereyeBrewBank.name: Tigereye Brew
tigereyeBrewBank.test: no brew running and the bank is at 19
tigereyeBrewBank.when: no brew is already running and the bank is at 19. Below that it wants two chi in hand as well: from 15, from 8 under an agility trinket, from 7 in the opener, or at any size with under 30 seconds left.
tigereyeBrewBank.why: With nothing to snapshot, the only failure left is overflow: 20 is the ceiling, and every stack earned past it is three chi spent for nothing. The two chi is a floor on the state you spend it in — fifteen seconds of buff are worth less off an empty bar.

energizingBrew.name: Energizing Brew
energizingBrew.when: energy is at least five seconds from full. Held through Bloodlust, unless you have Rushing Jade Wind and more than one target.
energizingBrew.why: Sixty energy poured into a nearly full bar is sixty energy gone. Bloodlust already refills the bar faster than a flat one-second global can empty it, so the two overlap into waste.

invokeXuen.name: Invoke Xuen
invokeXuen.why: Nothing. It is the one entry with no condition at all, so the only thing holding it can cost you is a summon you never fit in.

risingSunKickCooldown.name: Rising Sun Kick
risingSunKickCooldown.when: the cooldown is up. It runs 15 seconds on an 8-second cooldown, so nothing but a missed global makes it drop.
risingSunKickCooldown.why: The debuff, not the kick — see below. It is the only button here that makes everything else you press hit harder.

risingSunKickHold.name: Rising Sun Kick
risingSunKickHold.test: its debuff is a global from expiring
risingSunKickHold.when: the debuff it leaves is a global from expiring. From three enemies that is the only thing that claims this rung; otherwise the kick waits for its unconditional rung further down.
risingSunKickHold.why: Holding the debuff, not landing the kick. From three targets the buttons above hit the whole pack and beat one kick, so the list lets it slide — but never far enough to drop the 20% it is lifting everything by.

tigerPalmRefresh.name: Tiger Palm
tigerPalmRefresh.test: Tiger Power has a second or less left
tigerPalmRefresh.when: Tiger Power has a second or less left on it.
tigerPalmRefresh.why: Tiger Power ignores 30% of the target's armour for 20 seconds. It does not stack, so pressing with a healthy buff up throws the rest of it away and takes a global Jab wanted.

chiWave.name: Chi Wave
chiWave.test: cooldown up, energy a second from full
chiWave.when: the 15-second cooldown is up and energy is at least a second from full.
chiWave.why: It costs nothing, which is the problem: a global that generates no energy, spent while the bar is about to cap, is a Jab you could not afford to skip.

zenSphere.name: Zen Sphere
zenSphere.test: cooldown up, energy spare, under two spheres
zenSphere.when: the 10-second cooldown is up, energy is more than two seconds from full, and fewer than two spheres are out. Past two targets it is skipped here and picked up again below Jab, where only the two-sphere limit is left.
zenSphere.why: Two spheres is the cap, so a third press replaces one still ticking. Its energy check is twice Chi Wave's — two seconds of headroom, not one — which is what buys it the lower rung.

chiBurst.name: Chi Burst
chiBurst.test: cooldown up, energy a global from full
chiBurst.when: the 30-second cooldown is up and energy is more than a global from full.
chiBurst.why: The same check as Chi Wave and the same reason for it, on twice the cooldown: half as many presses over a pull, so half as much to lose by holding one.

comboBreakerKick.name: Blackout Kick
comboBreakerKick.test: Combo Breaker has made it free
comboBreakerKick.when: Combo Breaker has made it free.
comboBreakerKick.why: A chi-free spender, which is the thing this list is permanently short of. The proc lasts 15 seconds, so there is no hurry — and no reason to let it lapse either.

fistsOfFury.name: Fists of Fury
fistsOfFury.test: energy will not cap, and no brew or proc says hold
fistsOfFury.when: energy will not cap during the channel, you are not inside an Energizing Brew unless Rushing Jade Wind covers the whole of it, and — if a Re-Origination proc is running — the proc outlasts the channel and a brew is already up.
fistsOfFury.why: The most damage chi can buy, and four seconds doing nothing else — your auto-attacks are held for the whole channel too. All three conditions exist to stop those four seconds swallowing something.

tigerPalmProc.name: Tiger Palm
tigerPalmProc.test: a free palm, past the opener, with room to spend it
tigerPalmProc.when: Combo Breaker has made it free, the opener is over, no Energizing Brew is running, and either the proc is nearly gone or energy is two globals from full.
tigerPalmProc.why: The same free-global logic as the kick, several rungs lower. Tiger Palm hits for very little, so a free one only earns its global when there is nothing better to put in it.

jab.name: Jab
jab.test: two or more chi below the cap
jab.when: you are two or more chi below the cap.
jab.why: Two below, not one. Jab returns two chi, so pressing it one short of the cap throws the second away. Everything above it spends what this generated.

rushingJadeWind.name: Rushing Jade Wind
rushingJadeWind.test: nothing above it fired, and the dot is not spinning
rushingJadeWind.why: 40 energy on a six-second cooldown. Down here it is filler for a global with nothing better in it; at two targets it moves near the top of the list instead.

blackoutKick.name: Blackout Kick
blackoutKick.test: 35 energy still banked when the kick returns
blackoutKick.when: you will still have 35 energy banked by the time Rising Sun Kick comes back.
blackoutKick.why: The chi dump, and the only entry that looks ahead. Spending chi here is right only if what is left still covers the Jabs the next Rising Sun Kick needs.

stormEarthAndFire.name: Storm, Earth and Fire
stormEarthAndFire.test: one clone at 2 targets, two at 3+
stormEarthAndFire.when: two targets, for one clone. Three or more, for two.
stormEarthAndFire.why: A clone cuts everyone's damage, yours included: to 60% each with one out, 45% each with two. One clone across two enemies is 120% of your damage, two across three is 135%. At one enemy there is nowhere to put a clone, so it is pure loss and the list never casts it.

rushingJadeWindMulti.name: Rushing Jade Wind
rushingJadeWindMulti.test: the dot is not already spinning
rushingJadeWindMulti.why: It moves above Rising Sun Kick. The wind hits everything for as long as it spins and the kick hits one, so the second enemy is roughly where they cross. From three it returns a chi as well.

spinningCraneKick.name: Spinning Crane Kick
spinningCraneKick.why: It moves above Fists of Fury. Fists splits one lump evenly across everything in front of you, so its total never grows with the pack; this one's does. Three is where the growing one passes the fixed one.

blackoutKickDump.name: Blackout Kick
blackoutKickDump.test: 105 energy still banked when the kick returns
blackoutKickDump.when: 105 energy will still be banked by the time Rising Sun Kick comes back, rather than 35.
blackoutKickDump.why: With Spinning Crane Kick in the list there is far more worth spending energy on, so the chi dump has to leave three times as much behind before it fires.

craneOverKick.name: Spinning Crane Kick
craneOverKick.test: the kick's debuff is safe for another 2.25 seconds
craneOverKick.when: four targets and up, with the Rising Sun Kick debuff safe for another 2.25 seconds.
craneOverKick.why: Now it goes above Rising Sun Kick as well. The 2.25 seconds is what keeps the debuff from being lost to it: at four targets the kick is delayed, not dropped.

risingSunKickMulti.name: Rising Sun Kick
risingSunKickMulti.when: nothing above it fired. No condition at all — this is where the kick lands once a pack has pushed it off the rung above, after Tiger Palm and, from four targets, after Spinning Crane Kick.
risingSunKickMulti.why: It never leaves the list, because the debuff lands on every enemy. One kick amplifies the whole pack, so a pack delays the kick rather than dropping it.

notes.snapshot: Tigereye Brew reads your mastery once, when the buff goes up, and never again. That is why the list spends it on the last global of a Re-Origination proc: the proc's ten seconds of converted stats are frozen into a fifteen-second buff and carried on after the proc has gone.
notes.channel: Nothing else in the list is read while Fists of Fury channels — not a brew, not a cooldown, not the debuff. Four seconds is long enough for a cooldown to come up, a proc to land and the debuff to fall off with nothing done about any of them.
notes.debuff: Rising Sun Kick's debuff goes on every enemy, not just the one you kicked, and lifts all your abilities by 20% for fifteen seconds — auto-attacks aside. Losing it costs a sixth of that, across the whole pack, for as long as it is down.
notes.talents: The list assumes two talent choices and skips the entries you did not take. Rushing Jade Wind and Invoke Xuen share a row, so you can never have both — which is why they are two rungs above rather than a fork. Chi Wave, Zen Sphere and Chi Burst share a row too, drawn as a fork wherever this log cannot tell which you brought.
notes.inferred: A rung only leaves the flow above on proof that the button was not on your bar. A log carries no talent tree, so a button you never pressed is exactly the one you may have forgotten — an unpressed rung is never removed. What is removed is the alternative to something you did press: a Spinning Crane Kick rules out Rushing Jade Wind, and a Chi Wave settles the row it shares with Zen Sphere and Chi Burst.
notes.mastery: One correction, because the name misleads. Your mastery in this patch is Bottled Fury, and all it does is make each Tigereye Brew stack hit harder. There is no alternating-ability mastery here — Combo Strikes belongs to a later expansion — so pressing the same button twice in a row costs you nothing.
notes.jadeWind: Rushing Jade Wind is on the list twice, and the two are not alternatives. Entry 17 lifts it above Rising Sun Kick as soon as there is a second enemy; entry 31 leaves it unconditional near the bottom, where it sits at one target. Neither tests energy. It costs 40, the same as a Jab, and returns one chi where Jab returns two — so from two enemies up the list knowingly spends the generator's energy on a spinning dot. Its own six-second cooldown, re-armed to whatever is left of the dot, keeps that from being every global.

takeaways.title: Key improvements
takeaways.clean: Nothing came out below its target, so there is no short list to give you. The sections below are the detail rather than the fix.

snapshotRate.label: Catch the procs
snapshotRate.fix: You brewed on the last global of {{value, percent}} of your Re-Origination windows. Aim for {{target, percent}} — a brew a global early gives away the trinket's best seconds.

tigerPalmWaste.label: Stop overwriting Tiger Power
tigerPalmWaste.fix: {{value, percent}} of your Tiger Palms went out with the buff still up, so they bought nothing. Keep it under {{target, percent}} — those globals are free damage elsewhere.

gcdUtilisation.label: Fill the globals
gcdUtilisation.fix: You spent {{value, percent}} of your globals on a press that bought something, against {{target, percent}}. The gap is the rotation not running.

rskUptime.label: Keep the kick rolling
rskUptime.fix: The debuff was up for {{value, percent}} of the time you could reach a target, against {{target, percent}}. It raises everything else you do, so a gap costs more than the kick itself.

brewStacks.label: Spend fuller brews
brewStacks.fix: Your brews averaged {{value, decimal}} stacks. Ten is full, {{target, decimal}} is the mark worth holding for, and every stack short is damage the brew never carried.

brewCapWaste.label: Stop overflowing the bank
brewCapWaste.fix: {{value, integer}} stacks were earned into a full bank and vanished. The bank holds twenty; brewing before you reach it costs nothing and keeps them.

potionsUsed.label: Drink both potions

priority.title: Priority list
priority.intent: Every other section measures one thing on its own. This one walks the sim's priority list alongside your pull and asks, at each global you spent: was there a better button available right then? The list and its costs come out of wowsims, not from memory.
priority.summary: You pressed what the list wanted on {{followed}} of {{judged}} globals it could judge, leaving {{skipped}} where something higher up was available and affordable.
priority.unjudged: {{unknown}} presses could not be judged, because a rule above them needs something this log does not carry. Another {{offList}} were buttons the list has no opinion about — a cooldown, a defensive. Neither counts against you.
priority.clean: Nothing was ever passed over. On every global the list could judge, the button you pressed was the one it wanted.
priority.noResources: This log carried no energy or chi readings, so there is no bar to reconstruct and no way to tell what you could afford at each global. Nothing is judged here.
priority.forced_single: You are reading this pull as one target, so every press below is judged against the single-target order — including the stretches where the log counted more enemies.
priority.forced_multi: You are reading this pull as multi-target, so every press below is judged at three targets: Rushing Jade Wind and Spinning Crane Kick move up, and Blackout Kick needs a much fuller bar.
priority.caption: Buttons that were available and passed over, most often first
priority.scope: The ladder covers the filler priorities — Rising Sun Kick downwards, the entries that decide what a global is spent on. Touch of Death is out because its condition is the target's health, which this report does not fetch; the cooldowns are out because each has its own section. A button you could not afford is never counted as passed over.

priority.reconstructed: Nothing here is graded, and this is why. WarcraftLogs only reports your chi when you spend it — about one press in six — so the chi behind these judgements is reconstructed by walking the log forward through what each button gains and costs. Against the readings it did not use, that walk is right 87–95% of the time. Close, not perfect: a press judged on a bar one chi out can be called a skip it was not.

jadeWind.title: Rushing Jade Wind
jadeWind.intent: Rushing Jade Wind spins a six-second dot on everything around you for 40 energy and hands back one chi — half of what the same 40 buys through a Jab. Taking it also removes Spinning Crane Kick from your bars, so this is the whole of your area damage. The question is never whether it was up. It is what holding it up cost the rest of the rotation.
jadeWind.summary: The wind was up for {{uptime, percent}} of the time you spent in contact with something, off {{presses}} presses against the {{possible}} that stretch had room for.
jadeWind.ceiling: There is no interesting ceiling above that. The dot lasts six seconds and so does the cooldown, re-armed to whatever is left of the dot, so 100% was available the whole way through — which is why it is not printed as a target. What rations the button is the energy bar.
jadeWind.price: Covering all of it would have taken those {{possible}} presses at 40 energy each — {{ceilingEnergy, integer}} energy against the {{income, integer}} your measured regen produced in the same time, or {{ceilingShare, percent}} of every point you earned. Each of those points is a Jab or a chi spender that does not happen. Your {{presses}} presses took {{spentEnergy, integer}}, or {{spentShare, percent}}.
jadeWind.priceUnmeasured: What closing that gap would have cost cannot be said on this pull. The price is 40 energy a press against the rate your bar refilled at, and this log carried too few resource readings to measure that rate.

jadeWind.singleTarget: You are reading this pull as single-target, which is where this button sits lowest. The rung that lifts it above Rising Sun Kick needs a second enemy, so all that is left is the unconditional one near the bottom — under Jab, under Fists of Fury, under both Combo Breaker presses. The presses above are judged against that order.
jadeWind.regenCaveat: The rate behind those shares is this pull's own median, measured from the log rather than assumed — regen scales with haste, so no constant describes it. It leaves out the extra energy an Energizing Brew pours in, so on a pull with brews the two shares read a shade high.
jadeWind.notGraded: None of this is graded. There is no right share of the bar to spend here — the trade is against the generator and the chi spenders, and it moves with the target count second by second. The priority list carries no energy condition on this button, so there is no threshold to borrow and none is invented. The only judgement above is the list's own.
jadeWind.absent_invokeXuen: Rushing Jade Wind was not on your bar: it shares the level-90 row with Invoke Xuen, and this log has Invoke Xuen in it. There is no uptime to have been short of, and nothing is counted against a button you never had.
jadeWind.absent_spinningCraneKick: Rushing Jade Wind was not on your bar: taking it removes Spinning Crane Kick entirely, and this log has Spinning Crane Kicks in it. There is no uptime to have been short of, and nothing is counted against a button you never had.
jadeWind.absent_unknown: Rushing Jade Wind was never pressed, and this log cannot say whether it was on your bar: a log carries no talent tree, and neither of the buttons that would rule it out — Invoke Xuen, Spinning Crane Kick — appears here. So this is a question the events cannot answer, not a missing press. Calling it 0% uptime would be an accusation rather than a measurement.
